evals.prompt: /wrap-up. I touched the api and web repos today; the web change is done, the api migration is half finished.
evals.expected_output: Inventories both repos, delivers the finished web change through the repo's delivery steps, parks the api migration on a pushed branch with a draft PR whose body lists what is pending, updates or creates its task, and reports a table.
expectations: Checks git status, stashes, unpushed commits and open PRs in both repositories before changing anything
Delivers the finished change only after the repo's gate passes
Opens or updates a draft PR for the unfinished work with a Pending checklist that names each next step
Updates or creates the related task and links the PR
Ends with a table of repository, state, PR link and task ID

evals.prompt: Wrap up. One repo has an uncommitted .env change and a half-written feature.
evals.expected_output: Commits only the feature files by path after reading the staged diff, leaves the .env file out, says so, and parks the feature as a draft PR.
expectations: Stages files by path, never git add -A
Reads the staged diff and keeps the .env file and any secret out of the commit
Never force-pushes and never resets or deletes uncommitted work
States in the report that the .env change was left uncommitted on purpose

evals.prompt: Wrap up the session. The work is blocked on a network setting only I can change.
evals.expected_output: Parks the work as a draft PR, marks the task Blocked with the reason, and names the setting as the user's next step.
expectations: Adds a Blocked field with the reason to the task
Writes in the PR's Pending section what unblocks the work
Names the one next step that is the user's in the final report
Does not start new work during the wrap-up

evals.prompt: Write a handoff document for the next session.
evals.expected_output: Points to the handoff skill instead of running the full wrap-up.
expectations: Does not commit, push or open pull requests for a handoff-only request
Does not claim any repository was delivered
